sources.citation: Ravi Sankar S. Nair. 2013. Tribal Languages of Kerala. Language in India 13(7) (July 2013), 58 pp.
sources.note: Nothing about Allar. Sketches 13 Kerala tribal languages (Adiya, Aranadan, Bettakurumba, Cholanaickan, Irula, Kakkala, Kani, Kurichiya, Malamuthan, Malaveda, Mannan, Muduga, Mullukurumba); Allar is mentioned once ethnographically (p. 36, pollution distances from Malamuthan houses) and is not described.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 16th ed. Dallas: SIL International. Entry 'Allar' (Internet Archive copy 2010).
sources.note: Nothing. Classification 'Dravidian, Unclassified'; lexical similarity 61% with Malayalam, 59% with Tamil; population 350 (Shashi 1994); no dialects or phonology noted.

sources.citation: Sasikumar, M. 1996. 'Allar'. In T. Madhava Menon (chief ed.), The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, vol. II (entry between 'Adiyan' and 'Aranadan'). Thiruvananthapuram: International School of Dravidian Linguistics. ISBN 81-85692-16-5.
sources.note: No phonology. The only language content is the sentence that the Allar speak Malayalam 'with a peculiar intonation' plus some Tamil/Tulu loans (after Luiz 1962 and Mathur 1980 unpublished); nothing on word stress, accent placement or tone. Rest of the entry is ethnographic (habitat, material culture, kinship, ritual). Bibliography: Luiz 1962; Mathur PRG 1980 unpublished report.

sources.citation: Kareem, C. K. (comp.). 1986. Kerala District Gazetteers: Malappuram. Trivandrum: Government of Kerala, Kerala Gazetteers Department. Chapter IV 'People', pp. 249-251 ('Scheduled Tribes: Allars').
sources.note: No phonology; one sentence characterising Allar speech as Malayalam with 'peculiar intonation' and Tamil/Tulu admixture (derived from Luiz 1962). Nothing on stress or tone. Confirms that the ultimate source of all language remarks on Allar is Luiz 1962 pp. 32-35 (print only).

sources.citation: Somasekharan Nair, P. [c. 1983]. 'Tribes of Kerala: a proposal for reclassification' (Notes). International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics XII(2): 497 ff. Thiruvananthapuram: Dravidian Linguistics Association.
sources.note: No phonology content: a classificatory note on the naming/spelling of Kerala tribes by the University of Kerala linguist who led the tribal-language programme; gives only the name forms (aalaar, aallar, allar, 'Allar (Alan)'). Evidence that the Kerala tribal-linguistics school knew the group but published no sketch of its speech.
